topics.name: Section A Reading: unseen 19th-century prose fiction (1.1)
points: Reading and understanding a range of prose fiction, including an unseen 19th-century extract
Question 1: identify information from a given part of the extract (AO1, 1 mark)
Question 2: give two ways the writer shows something (AO2, 2 marks)
Question 3: analyse how the writer uses language and structure (AO2, 6 marks)
Question 4: evaluate how successfully an effect is achieved, with reference to the whole text (AO4, 15 marks)
Drawing and justifying inferences; evaluating evidence, usefulness and bias
Summarising the main themes and ideas from a single text
Using accurate subject terminology when analysing vocabulary, grammar, form and structure

topics.name: Section B Imaginative writing (1.2)
points: Question 5 or 6: imaginative writing task linked by theme to the reading extract; optional image prompts (40 marks)
Writing to describe and narrate; using language imaginatively and creatively
Maintaining a consistent point of view and organising text for impact
Rhetorical devices, e.g. rhetorical questions, antithesis and parenthesis
Communicating clearly and imaginatively for audience and purpose (AO5, 24 marks)
Vocabulary, sentence structures, spelling and punctuation (AO6, 16 marks)

topics.name: Section A Reading: two unseen 20th- and 21st-century non-fiction texts (2.1)
points: Text types: journalism (articles, reviews), speeches, journals, reference book extracts, literary non-fiction (autobiography, letters, travel writing)
Questions 1, 2, 4 and 5: identify and interpret information from Text 1 and Text 2 (AO1, 1 to 2 marks)
Question 3: analyse how the writer uses language and structure in Text 1 (AO2, 15 marks)
Question 6: evaluate how successfully the writer achieves an effect in Text 2 (AO4, 15 marks)
Question 7(a): synthesise evidence from both texts, e.g. similarities (AO1, 6 marks)
Question 7(b): compare writers' ideas and perspectives and how they are presented (AO3, 14 marks)
Critical reading: identifying bias and misuse of evidence; reading texts in context

topics.name: Section B Transactional writing (2.2)
points: Question 8 or 9: transactional writing task linked by theme to the reading texts (40 marks)
Forms: article, letter, review, speech text, section of a guide, textbook, leaflet or booklet
Writing to explain, instruct, inform, respond and argue for a specified audience and purpose
Selecting and emphasising key ideas; citing evidence and quotation; creating emotional impact
Communicating clearly and organising ideas for audience and purpose (AO5, 24 marks)
Vocabulary, sentence structures, spelling and punctuation (AO6, 16 marks)

topics.name: Spoken Language endorsement (non-exam assessment)
points: Selecting and organising information and ideas for a prepared formal presentation, agreed in advance with the teacher
Planning for different purposes and audiences; presentation formats (talk, speech, debate or dialogue)
Giving the presentation in a formal setting (up to about ten minutes)
Listening and responding appropriately to questions and feedback
Using spoken Standard English
Pass, Merit and Distinction criteria; graded separately and not part of the 9 to 1 grade
